literal: " Xing Gong's younger brother Xing Ru was also clever and precocious; late in Wuping he was appointed assistant in the Writings Office.
idiomatic: " Xing Gong's younger brother Xing Ru was clever and precocious too; late in Wuping he served as an assistant in the Writings Office.

literal: Zhao Yanshen was a man of Wan in Nanyang, a descendant of Han Grand Tutor Xi.
idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen came from Wan in Nanyang, a descendant of Han Grand Tutor Zhao Xi.

literal: His great-grandfather Nan was prefect of Qinghe; his kindly governance made the family settle there; Qinghe was later changed to Pingyuan, so he was reckoned a man of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Nan had been prefect of Qinghe; his fair rule made the family settle there. Qinghe was later renamed Pingyuan, so they counted as men of Pingyuan.

literal: His original name was Yin; to avoid the Qi temple taboo he took his courtesy name as his public name.
idiomatic: His original name was Yin; to avoid the Qi temple taboo he went by his courtesy name instead.

literal: His father Fengbo held office in Wei as secretariat gentleman and acting magistrate of Luoyang.
idiomatic: His father Fengbo had served Wei as secretariat gentleman and acting magistrate of Luoyang.

literal: When Yanshen became eminent, [Fengbo] was posthumously invested as minister of works.
idiomatic: Once Yanshen rose to prominence, Fengbo was posthumously made minister of works.

literal: Yanshen was orphaned young and poor, and served his mother with extreme filial piety.
idiomatic: Yanshen lost his father early and grew up poor, yet served his mother with fierce devotion.

literal: At age ten he once called on Minister over the Masses Cui Guang.
idiomatic: At ten he once called on Minister over the Masses Cui Guang.

literal: Guang said to the guests: "The ancients read the whites of the eyes to know men — this one will surely go far.
idiomatic: Guang told the guests, "The ancients read the whites of the eyes to know a man — this boy will go far.

literal: " By nature he was intelligent and quick, skilled at writing and reckoning, peaceful and devoted to the Way, not mingling in social rounds — refined opinionists looked up to him.
idiomatic: " He was bright and quick by nature, skilled at writing and reckoning, easy in manner and devoted to the Way, and kept out of casual company — men of taste deferred to him.

literal: At daybreak he would sweep outside the gate himself, not letting others see — he made it his constant habit.
idiomatic: Each dawn he swept outside the gate himself and would not let others watch — he made it a daily habit.

literal: At first he was a menial guest of Minister over the Masses Sima Ziru, supplying copy work.
idiomatic: At first he was a lowly guest of Minister over the Masses Sima Ziru, hired to copy documents.

literal: Ziru was pleased that he made no mistakes and wanted to bring him in to view the administration quarters.
idiomatic: Ziru was pleased that he never erred and meant to bring him inside to see the offices.

literal: Yin wore boots without felt lining, hat and clothes worn and tattered — Ziru supplied him.
idiomatic: Yin wore unlined boots and threadbare hat and clothes; Ziru furnished him.

literal: He was employed as a clerical officer in the secretariat, and after a month was promoted to regular clerical officer.
idiomatic: He was made a secretariat clerical officer and, after a month, promoted to regular clerical officer.

literal: Gao Huan was at Jinyang and asked for the two histories; Ziru recommended Yanshen.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was at Jinyang and asked for the two histories; Ziru recommended Yanshen.

literal: Later he was appointed Ziru's metropolitan administration staff officer, and was leap-promoted to director of the water section.
idiomatic: Later he was made Ziru's metropolitan administration staff officer, then leap-promoted to director of the water section.

literal: When Gao Cheng became Minister over the Masses and oversaw selection, he culled the various bureau directors — Yanshen, because of low birth, was dismissed to be Administrator in Support of Cangzhou, and he declined and did not go.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng became Minister over the Masses and took charge of selection, he culled the bureau directors. Yanshen, judged too humble in origin, was sent out as administrator in support of Cangzhou; he declined and would not go.

literal: Ziru spoke to Gao Huan; he was summoned and made staff officer for merit affairs in the Great Chancellor's office, exclusively handling secrets; most documents came from his hand, and he was called quick and responsive.
idiomatic: Ziru spoke to Gao Huan; Yanshen was summoned and made staff officer for merit affairs in the Great Chancellor's office, handling secrets alone. Most papers passed through his hand, and men called him quick and sure.

literal: Gao Huan once sat facing him and ordered him to draft a military command; he stroked Yanshen's forehead and said: "If Heaven grants you years, you will surely reach great heights.
idiomatic: Gao Huan once sat facing him and ordered a military command drafted; he stroked Yanshen's forehead and said, "If Heaven grants you years, you will go far.

literal: " He often told Minister over the Masses Sun Teng: "Yanshen is careful and reverent beyond anything in antiquity."
idiomatic: " He often told Minister over the Masses Sun Teng, "Yanshen is careful and reverent beyond anything in antiquity."

literal: When Gao Huan died they concealed the mourning; Gao Cheng feared trouble in Henan and went to inspect on his own, entrusting the aftermath to Yanshen and making him metropolitan administration section director.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan died the mourning was kept secret. Gao Cheng feared trouble in Henan and went to inspect in person, leaving the aftermath to Yanshen and making him metropolitan administration section director.

literal: When about to depart he clasped hands and wept: "I entrust my mother and younger brother to you — may I have this heart.
idiomatic: As he was leaving he clasped Yanshen's hands and wept: "I entrust my mother and younger brother to you — trust that my heart is with you.

literal: " Thereupon inside and outside were quiet — Yanshen's doing.
idiomatic: " Inside and outside thereupon grew quiet — Yanshen's doing.

literal: When [Gao Cheng] returned to announce the mourning he praised him greatly, opened the register of commanderies and counties for selections, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Anguo county.
idiomatic: When he returned to announce the mourning he praised Yanshen at length, opened the commandery-and-county register for selection, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Anguo county.

literal: On the campaign at Yingchuan they diverted water to flood the city; the battlements would soon be submerged, yet Western Wei general Wang Sizheng still wanted to fight to the death.
idiomatic: On the Yingchuan campaign they diverted water to flood the city; the battlements would soon go under, yet Western Wei general Wang Sizheng still meant to fight to the death.

literal: Gao Cheng ordered Yanshen to enter the city alone to persuade; that same day they surrendered, and he personally led Sizheng out by the hand.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent Yanshen into the city alone to persuade them; that same day they surrendered, and he led Sizheng out by the hand.

literal: Earlier, Gao Cheng had said to Yanshen: "Last night I dreamed of hunting and met a herd of swine; I shot and took them all, but one great boar I could not get.
idiomatic: Earlier Gao Cheng had told Yanshen, "Last night I dreamed I was hunting and met a herd of swine; I shot and took them all, but one great boar I could not get.

literal: You said you would take it for me — in a moment you had the boar and came in.
idiomatic: You said you would take it for me — and in a moment you had the boar and came in.

literal: " At this Gao Cheng laughed: "The dream is fulfilled.
idiomatic: " Now Gao Cheng laughed: "The dream is fulfilled.

literal: " Thereupon he removed Sizheng's belt dagger and gave it to Yanshen, saying: "May you always win such profit."
idiomatic: " He then took Sizheng's belt dagger and gave it to Yanshen, saying, "May you always win such profit."

literal: Yanshen served successive courts, constantly in close counsel, gentle and cautious, joy and anger never showing on his face.
idiomatic: Yanshen served successive reigns, always near the inner counsel, gentle and cautious, never letting joy or anger show on his face.

literal: From Huangjian onward his treatment grew somewhat heavier; whenever summoned he might ascend the imperial couch; he was often called by office title and not by personal name.
idiomatic: From Huangjian on his honors grew weightier; when summoned he might even mount the imperial couch, and the emperor often called him by office title rather than by name.

literal: In all selections he would first weigh and fix the list, promoting persons by conduct first — the frivolous were never enrolled.
idiomatic: In every appointment he weighed candidates first and promoted men of character; the frivolous never made his list.

literal: After Emperor Xiaozhao took hold of court power, many ministers privately urged accession; Yanshen alone did not speak.
idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozhao seized court power, many ministers privately urged him to take the throne; Yanshen alone kept silent.

literal: Xiaozhao once said to Wang Xi: "If the crowd says everyone's heart agrees the empire has its destination, why have you never heard Yanshen say so?
idiomatic: Xiaozhao once said to Wang Xi, "If men say all hearts agree the realm has found its lord, why have you never heard Yanshen say so?

literal: " Xi told him; Yanshen could not refuse further and submitted a memorial urging it — such was how the times valued him.
idiomatic: " Xi told Yanshen; unable to refuse further, Yanshen submitted a memorial urging accession — such was the weight he carried in his age.

literal: He was habitually yielding and self-restraining, never treating others with arrogance — hence he might leave office and return again.
idiomatic: He was habitually yielding and restrained, never arrogant toward others — so he might leave office and be called back again.

literal: His mother, née Fu, was refined in conduct and judgment.
idiomatic: His mother, Lady Fu, was refined in conduct and judgment.

literal: When Yanshen was three, Fu was already a widow; the family wished her to remarry, but she swore she would die first.
idiomatic: When Yanshen was three, Lady Fu was already a widow; the family wanted her to remarry, but she swore she would die first.

literal: When Yanshen was five, Fu said to him: "The house is poor and you are small — how can we get by?
idiomatic: When Yanshen was five, Lady Fu said to him, "We are poor and you are small — how can we live?

literal: " Yanshen wept and said: "If Heaven pities us, when I grow up I shall repay you looking up.
idiomatic: " Yanshen wept and said, "If Heaven takes pity, when I am grown I shall repay you on my knees.

literal: " Fu was moved by his intent and wept facing him.
idiomatic: " Lady Fu was moved by his words and wept with him.

literal: When Yanshen was appointed grand master of ceremonies and returned, he did not remove court dress but went first to see his mother, kneeling and stating that from childhood he was orphaned and exposed, yet through her instruction had come to this.
idiomatic: When Yanshen was made grand master of ceremonies and returned, he did not change out of court dress but went first to his mother, knelt, and said that as a small orphan he had come to this only through her teaching.

literal: Mother and son wept together a long while, then only did he change clothes.
idiomatic: Mother and son wept together a long while before he changed his clothes.

literal: Later she was made grand princess dowager of Yiyang.
idiomatic: Later she was made grand princess dowager of Yiyang.

literal: Yanshen had seven sons; Zhongjiang was the notable one.
idiomatic: Yanshen had seven sons; Zhongjiang was the one of note.

literal: Zhongjiang was deep and keen with his father's air, warm, mild, respectful and thrifty — even toward wife and children he never slackened, solemn all day.
idiomatic: Zhongjiang was deep and keen with his father's manner, warm, mild, respectful and thrifty — even with wife and children he never slackened, grave all day long.

literal: He studied widely among books and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.
idiomatic: He read widely and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.

literal: Though writing letters to his younger brothers, the characters were in proper regular script; he said cursive cannot be left unlearned, but to use it on people is like slighting them lightly; yet with junior kin in the household one fears they will suspect one should naturally write that way — so one must use clerical script.
idiomatic: Even in letters to his younger brothers he wrote in proper regular script. He said cursive must be mastered, yet to use it on others is to treat them lightly; with juniors in the household one fears they will think that is simply how one should write to them — so the brush must be clerical.

literal: Yanshen begged transfer to grant his son the enfeoffment as viscount of Wannian county.
idiomatic: Yanshen asked that his own enfeoffment be transferred to make his son viscount of Wannian county.

literal: He held posts as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.
idiomatic: He served as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was director of the personnel section, and ended as governor of Anzhou.
idiomatic: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he was director of the personnel section and ended as governor of Anzhou.

literal: Among Northern Qi chancellors, only Yanshen began well and ended well.
idiomatic: Among Northern Qi chancellors, only Yanshen began well and ended well.

literal: Yet he urged the court to make his son Shujian secretariat vice director — this drew considerable talk.
idiomatic: Yet he pressed the court to make his son Shujian secretariat vice director, which drew sharp talk.

literal: At the time Feng Zicong's son Ciming and Zu Ting's son Junxin in succession held posts in the secretariat, so the saying ran: "Feng, Zu, and Zhao are befouling our phoenix pool.
idiomatic: At the time Feng Zicong's son Ciming and Zu Ting's son Junxin took the secretariat in turn, so people said, "Feng, Zu, and Zhao — they're fouling the phoenix pool.

literal: " Yet Shujian's physique was the worst of all.
idiomatic: " Of the three, Shujian's looks were the worst.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
